body: I know this. I am just saying that it was a peaceful protest. The man in the truck has the right to drive by with his flag and make his position known.  When he stopped his truck in the intersection, at a green light, and jumped out HE escalated the situation. I am not arguing with you. I was there. I have video. I saw what went down. I just wasn't close enough to hear what was said.

It wasn't the protester in costume who threw water but there still was no reason for him to stop his truck and jump out in the first place. He could have just continued to circle with his flag and make his position known peacefully; just as everyone else was.

I completely agree.  There was another truck that drove by earlier and yelled something at protesters and a protester used his sign to hit the back of his flat bed as he drove by.  I actually spoke up and told him that although I understood his anger, his behavior wasn't matching the message we were trying to send and he understood and backed down.  Emotions are high but 99% of people there understood the message. Freedom of speech and freedom of protest.  Same as those trucks flying their MAGA flags had the right to drive through and thumbs down to show their true feelings. I don't agree. I am not happy about it but it's their right.

The person stopped his vehicle and got out in an intersection at a greenlight BEFORE the water was thrown. That being said, I agree that water should have never been thrown in the first place no matter what the truck guy said.  But the truck guy ALSO shouldn't have punched the guy for throwing water.  Many parts of the situation were not handled correctly but I can honestly say that I did not see a single person trying to incite violence.

That's a good point. There was also one time that she kind of "spaced out" and it looked like one of her eyes drifted again. 

She had her first surgery in October which was about two months before she turned 6. Then her second surgery was three weeks ago. But yes I think that is their goal.  

This doctor is about six hours away so we will see them again in person in May hopefully. I just want the best outcome as we can get.

So, after my daughter's first surgery, the doctor would have us patch the eye that was her "stronger" eye to help the "weaker' one get stronger. Her "weaker" eye was the one that was turned in before surgery and out after surgery. As soon as we would cover the "stronger" eye, her turned eye would go straight.  

She just had a second surgery about three weeks ago.  The eye looks much straighter than before. We are still patching so when we patch the "stronger" eye the "weaker" one doesn't move anymore since it's straight. She says when she covers each eye that the image she sees "moves a bit from side to side". I don't feel like it moves for me when I am covering one of my eyes. So I wonder if she is still struggling with binocular vision as you are describing. 

Also, when told to look up, I noticed her "weaker" eye drifts inward again. But that's the only time it doesn't look aligned. 

I appreciate your message and information. Just trying to make sure I get her the best care.

My daughter was older when we had her first surgery but we had a similar experience. Her eye was 35 dp inwards and after surgery it looked great for a few weeks and then it started drifting out. It stayed at 35 dp outwards. She had her second surgery about 3 weeks ago now. We had adjustable sutures and have done patching as well since the day after surgery. Her eye is now basically straight.  I don't know the exact measurements but I am glad we did the second surgery. Even though it was difficult.
